prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep Pd-catalysed C-N coupling as my preferred prize. It is one reaction class, made general through mechanism-driven ligand design: Buchwald's biaryl phosphines and Hartwig's hindered alkyl phosphines, with the oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination steps worked out independently by two groups. It has more than two decades of independent confirmation and is used daily in discovery and process chemistry to make aryl amines, one of the commonest motifs in medicines and materials. The attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist: two independent programmes and no forced exclusions. Kosugi's aminostannane chemistry is a genuine precursor but was stoichiometric in tin and not general, so a citation worded around general catalytic C-N coupling handles it without a priority ruling. After the first round I have not changed my configuration. I have changed how I describe the choice. It is not mature versus new. It is a settled discovery with settled credit against a very promising one whose credit and citation the committee has not yet agreed.
statement.case_against: The reservation I take most seriously is the 2010 prize. Several colleagues, including Linke and Sparr, see amination as an extension of a recognised field, and my answer that C-N bond formation needed a different ligand and mechanistic solution is a judgement and not a proof. A committee that values a new mode of action over a late, clean methodology prize would reasonably choose B023, and the chair's summary shows six of eight members doing so. Kosugi's exclusion is defensible but will be criticised. A pure synthetic-methodology prize is also narrower in scope than a new drug modality, and degraders in the clinic could well make B023 the obvious choice within a few years.

responses.point: Sparr moved to B023 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, now weighs the missing approved degrader less, and says C-N coupling extends the cross-coupling chemistry honoured in 2010 whereas degradation introduces a different mode of action.
responses.response: I agree that approval is not the test and I do not claim B023 is premature on that ground alone. My problem is the citation. Her configuration credits Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target together with the PROTAC concept, and those two strands have separate origins: one is a designed bifunctional molecule, the other a mechanism found for an existing drug. One sentence that covers both will either be vague or leave out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim, whose claims she lists herself. On the 2010 point, I do not see how novelty of mode of action is the only measure, since a new reactivity solution at the amine-binding and C-N reductive elimination steps is also a conceptual advance, only a smaller one. I accept that this is where we differ, and I would not call her choice unreasonable.

responses.point: Linke prefers B023 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, names B002 as his first alternative, and frames the choice as a late, safe achievement against a fresher conceptual one, putting more weight on novelty and accepting B002 if immaturity counts against B023.
responses.response: I do not think late and safe describes it well. The amination reaction came out of two decades of ligand and mechanism work and it still enables new chemistry each year. His own conditional acceptance of B002 is useful, and I take it as a sign that B002 is something the committee can agree on. I would then ask him the chair's own question in reverse: if the committee cannot agree whether the third name is Handa or Ciulli, or whether PROTACs and glues share a citation, would he treat that unresolved credit as a reason to prefer the configuration with no open attribution question? I would, and I regard that as a scientific point about how well defined the achievement is, not only a procedural one.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers B023 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, argues that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs a general platform and that cereblon is a target-identification result, and names B002 as his safer alternative if the committee cannot settle the allocation.
responses.response: His reading of the third name is the one I find most convincing, and in my round-1 response I said that if the committee goes to B023 his structural argument favours Ciulli. I would add a consequence he does not draw. If Handa is dropped and the citation is narrowed to designed bifunctional degraders, the glue half of the field is left out and the Handa supporters, who include five members, may not accept it. His own caveat that B002 is the safer choice if allocation cannot be settled is the point I most agree with. If a configuration for B023 is chosen, my preference would be Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a citation limited to PROTACs.

responses.point: Zou keeps B002 first because it is the only top candidate whose discovery and credit are both settled, asks that Kosugi's precedence be handled in the citation wording, and admits she may be underweighting the novelty of a new drug modality.
responses.response: I agree on the wording. The citation should say general catalytic C-N cross-coupling, so that it is distinct from 2010 and does not rule on Kosugi's earlier stoichiometric work. I do not think we need to add Kosugi as a third name. That would turn a clean two-person attribution into a contested one, and his tin-amide reaction was neither catalytic in the modern sense nor general. Where I would be more cautious than she is: B023 should not be called conceptually fresher in a way that settles the question. Fresh and well defined are different properties, and in the first round I did not see a single sentence that covers PROTACs, glues, Ciulli and Handa without leaving a strong claim outside.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept C-N coupling as a distinct achievement from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize, or whether the overlap is decisive for five or more members.
Whether Kosugi's precursor work should be acknowledged in the wording of the citation, or whether leaving him out will be seen as a priority error.

Whether PROTACs and cereblon-dependent glues are one discovery or two. I lean toward two, but I accept that this view is held by only a few members and I may be setting the bar for a single citation too high.

Whether I am discounting the clinical trajectory of degraders. If the committee reads the evidence as sufficient and settles on a clear three-name set, I would regard B023 as a legitimate prize and not as an error.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal to disclose. I am a synthetic organic chemist at Lund with colleagues Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr, but none of the shortlisted candidates is connected to Lund, KTH, Chalmers, Tartu or my mentor Masamune. I have no personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi, Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli or any other shortlisted person.
